transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

Since you have already cleaned the filter and it still isn’t draining, the issue is likely not a clogged filter but rather one of the following components. Here’s a step-by-step diagnostic guide to help you identify which part needs replacement:

### 1. Drain Pump (Most Likely Cause)
• Symptoms: You may hear a humming sound when the drain cycle starts, but no water comes out. Or, there is complete silence.
• Check:
• Listen during the drain phase. If you hear a hum but no water movement, the pump impeller may be jammed or broken.
• Visually inspect the pump (behind the filter housing) for debris like coins, buttons, or lint that might have bypassed the filter and jammed the impeller.
• Solution: If the impeller is broken, clogged internally, or electrically faulty, you need a new drain pump.

### 2. Drain Hose
• Symptoms: Water backs up into the drum or doesn’t exit at all.
• Check:
• Disconnect the hose from the back of the washer and check for kinks, clogs, or siphoning issues.
• Ensure the hose isn’t pushed too far down the standpipe (which can cause airlock).
• Solution: Clear any blockage or replace if damaged.

### 3. Pressure Switch / Pressure Sensor
• Symptoms: The washer runs through cycles but doesn’t drain or spin, even though there’s water in the drum. It may also display an error code (e.g., E15, F05, or similar depending on your region).
• Check:
• Inspect the thin plastic tube connected to the pressure switch for kinks, cracks, or water trapped inside.
• If the tube is clear but the washer still doesn’t drain, the pressure sensor itself may be faulty and not signaling the control board that the tub is full (or empty).
• Solution: Replace the pressure hose if damaged, or replace the pressure switch/sensor.

### 4. Control Board / Main PCB
• Symptoms: No response from the pump despite good power supply, or multiple unrelated errors.
• Check:
• Use a multimeter to check for voltage at the drain pump terminals during the drain cycle. If voltage is present but the pump doesn’t run, the pump is faulty (see #1). If no voltage is present, the control board may not be sending the signal.
• Solution: Replace the control board only if all other components are confirmed working.

### 5. Door Lock / Interlock Switch
• Symptoms: The washer won’t drain or spin because it doesn’t think the door is securely locked.
• Check:
• Ensure the door latches properly. Listen for a click when closing. If the machine displays an error code related to the door (e.g., E10, F04), this may be the issue.
• Solution: Replace the door lock assembly.

---

### 🔧 Recommended Next Steps:
1. Check for Error Codes: Look at your display for any codes (e.g., E15, F05, etc.) and consult your manual. This will narrow it down significantly.
2. Test the Pump:
• Unplug the washer.
• Access the pump (usually behind the filter housing).
• Manually spin the impeller—it should turn freely. If it’s stuck or broken, replace the pump.
• If it spins freely but doesn’t drain when powered, test for voltage during the drain cycle.
3. Inspect the Pressure Hose: Ensure it’s not kinked or clogged with water/mold.

### ✅ Most Common Fix:
In most cases where the filter is clean and draining fails, the drain pump is the culprit. Start by replacing that if you’re comfortable doing DIY repairs. If you’re unsure, consider calling a technician to diagnose whether it’s electrical (control board/sensor) or mechanical (pump/hose).

ok, I looked and the display shows E18 when it stalls. pump hums but no water moves, and the hose behind looks fine. so is it the pump?

Yes, based on your symptoms, it is almost certainly the drain pump.

Here’s why:
• Error Code E18: On many Bosch washers (including models like the WAW series), E18 specifically indicates a "Drainage problem" or "Pump blocked/faulty."
• Hums but no water movement: This is the classic sign of a jammed pump impeller or a failed motor. The pump is trying to run (hence the hum), but something is physically preventing it from spinning, or the internal motor windings are burnt out.

### ✅ Next Steps: Replace the Drain Pump

#### 🔧 How to Confirm Before Buying:
1. Unplug the washer.
2. Remove the filter cover again and locate the pump behind it (usually held by 3–4 screws).
3. Disconnect the electrical connector from the pump.
4. Try to manually spin the impeller (you may need to reach in with a finger or small tool through the filter opening). If it’s stiff, stuck, or broken, the pump is faulty.
5. Check for any hidden debris (coins, hairpins, etc.) lodged in the impeller housing that might have been missed when cleaning the filter.

#### 🛒 What to Buy:
• Part Name: Bosch Drain Pump
• Common Part Numbers:
• `00672819` (very common for many Bosch models)
• `00493530`
• `00672818`
• ⚠️ Important: Double-check your exact model number (FD 9409) on the rating plate inside the door or on the back of the machine. Use that to verify compatibility with a retailer like:
• Bosch Parts Direct
• PartSelect
• Amazon (search "Bosch FD 9409 drain pump")

#### 🔧 Replacement Difficulty:
• Easy–Moderate: You’ll need basic tools (screwdriver, pliers).
• Steps:
  1. Unplug washer and turn off water supply.
  2. Place towels/basin under the filter area to catch residual water.
  3. Remove the pump screws and disconnect hoses/wiring.
  4. Install new pump, reconnect, and test.

ok did the finger check, impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. the E-Nr on the label is rubbed off so I can't read it, only the FD 9409. so which pump do I order?

The "stiff and gritty" feeling confirms that debris has worked its way past the filter and into the pump housing, causing friction. Even if the impeller still turns, this grit will likely cause premature failure or continued poor drainage. You need to replace the pump.

### 🔍 How to Find the Correct Pump Without the E-Nr

Since your E-Nr (the 8–10 digit Bosch engineering number) is unreadable, you have two reliable options:

#### ✅ Option 1: Use Your Model Number + Visual Confirmation (Recommended)
Your model FD 9409 likely corresponds to a Bosch WAW series washer (common in Europe). The most common drain pump for this era/model range is:

🔹 Bosch Drain Pump Part No.: `00672819`
(Also sometimes listed as `BSH 00672819` or `0067281900`)

But to be 100% sure before ordering:
1. Remove the old pump carefully (you can do this without fully disassembling the machine):
• Unplug the washer.
• Open the filter door and remove the filter.
• Locate the pump behind it (usually held by 3–4 screws).
• Disconnect the electrical plug and loosen the hose clamps on the inlet/outlet hoses.
• Pull the pump out just enough to see the part number printed on the pump housing itself (often molded into the plastic or on a label).

2. Cross-reference that number:
• Common Bosch pump numbers for this model range:
• `00672819` ✅ Most likely
• `00493530`
• `00672818`
• `166208`

#### ✅ Option 2: Search by Model + "Drain Pump" on a Parts Site
Go to one of these sites and enter FD 9409:
• Bosch Parts Direct
• PartSelect
• Amazon (search: "Bosch FD 9409 drain pump")

Look for a pump that matches the shape, hose connections, and electrical connector of your current one.

### 🛒 What to Order
If you can’t remove it right now, order this widely compatible part and double-check visually:
👉 Bosch Drain Pump `00672819`

It fits most Bosch/Washer/Dryer models from the 2010s–2020s with similar drainage systems.

### 🔧 Pro Tip When Installing the New Pump
• Clean the pump housing area thoroughly before installing the new pump to remove any grit left behind.
• Ensure the impeller spins freely by hand before reconnecting power.
• Run a drain/spin cycle empty to test for leaks and proper function.

I can't read the E-Nr and I'm not taking the machine apart beyond the filter, no tools for the sump. So is 00672819 definitely the one, or not? Just need one part number I can trust.

You’re right to be cautious—without seeing the pump or reading the E-Nr, no single part number can be guaranteed 100% correct. However:

### ✅ Most Likely Part for FD 9409:
Bosch Drain Pump `00672819`
This is the most common drain pump used in Bosch front-load washers from your era, including models like WAW28540GB, WAX32540GB, and similar FD-series machines. It fits the vast majority of Bosch/Euro-style front loaders with a rear-drain configuration.

### ⚠️ But Here’s the Catch:
Bosch has used three very similar-looking pumps in recent years:
1. `00672819` – Most common, 3-prong connector, standard hose clamps
2. `00493530` – Slightly different mounting or connector
3. `00672818` – Older variant

### 🛡️ Safe Bet:
If you want one part number to order and hope it fits, go with:
👉 `00672819`

But please note: If it doesn’t fit, you’ll need to either:
• Return/exchange it (most retailers allow this if uninstalled)
• Or remove the old pump just enough to read its number (takes 5 minutes with a screwdriver and pliers—no full disassembly needed).

### 🔍 Quick Visual Check When It Arrives:
Before installing, compare:
• Connector shape & pin count
• Hose inlet/outlet positions
• Mounting screw pattern

If those match your current pump, it’s the right one.
